data.explanation: 10 role-complete bundles (baseline included) x 14 frozen oracle cases x 2 repeats: 280 calls, 0 retries. Bundle r4-a2-c2 is the top-ranked semantically accepted set: 84/84 role cells, 28/28 threshold-0 verdicts, 14/14 stable cases, zero regressions against the baseline. Confidence is diagnostic only; production review keeps the 0.6 threshold. Tuner rationale: round 1 (preserved in round-1/, same frozen oracle, 15 bundles, 420 calls) accepted none; every bead-level relevant override answered relevant=no on the pass fixture, because the fixture describes what tool code calls and does not literally state a code change, and the baseline answered relevant=no on both sc-agent crate probes and relevant=yes on the topical note. Round 2's r4 relevant override counts an item that says what scoped code calls, uses or is generated from, and answers no for docs, CI, tracker and discussion work. Production caveat (diagnostic, selection unchanged): for this prohibition anchor, relevance and conflict gate the verdict. The sealed c2 contradicted question answered no at 0.28/0.33 on the compliant probe, which is below the 0.6 production threshold and would make that item underspecified. Rank 2, r4-cur-cur, kept every relevance and conflict cell at 0.67 or higher. Its low cells were on addressed, which does not gate a prohibition.

criteria.no: The item says nothing about sharing one implementation: it is silent, adds tool-specific code, only mentions the topic, or copies code.
criteria.unclear: The item hints at sharing but it cannot be told whether one shared implementation is used.
criteria.yes: The item says two or more files, crates or tools use one shared implementation (for example 'both tools call the shared client generated from the template', 'move the duplicated parser into the shared module', 'regenerate the client in both tools from the shared template').

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state or plan that logic shared by files, crates or tools lives in one place they all use (a shared module, crate, or the client template from which code is generated), or that existing duplicated logic is moved into such a place? Judge presence of that statement only, not conflict. An item that simply does not copy anything but says nothing about shared logic has not stated it.

criteria.no: The item plans no such copy: it is silent, shares one implementation, generates code from one template, or adds logic with no counterpart elsewhere.
criteria.unclear: The item could be read as duplicating logic, but it is ambiguous.
criteria.yes: The item plans to copy, paste, duplicate, port or vendor a function, parser or other logic from one file, crate or tool into another.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan to copy, paste, duplicate, port or vendor logic from one file, crate or tool into another, so the same logic exists in two places? Regenerating code from one shared template is not copying. An item that is silent about copying does not plan it.

criteria.no: The item's work involves no such source code: it is documentation, a plan note, CI or workflow configuration, tracker work, a discussion, or code elsewhere.
criteria.unclear: The item refers to code too vaguely to tell whether it is source in these crates, tools or the template.
criteria.yes: The item adds, changes, copies, regenerates or wires source code in an sc-agent crate (crates/sc-agent*, crates/decidr or another crates/ member), judge-jev, plan-anchor, or the client template both tools use, or says what such code calls, uses, shares or is generated from.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` concern source code in an sc-agent crate (crates/sc-agent*, crates/decidr or another crates/ member), judge-jev, plan-anchor, or the client template both tools use? It does when the item adds, changes, copies, ports, vendors, regenerates or wires that code, including an item that says what that code calls, uses, shares or is generated from (for example 'judge-jev and plan-anchor both call the shared client', 'add a field to a struct in crates/sc-agent-records'). It does not when the item's work is only documentation, plan notes, CI or workflow configuration, tracker housekeeping or a discussion, even if it names these tools or mentions duplication.
